root_corrections_accepted.repair: A guardian process now owns the connection and monitors the actual caller, and issues exit(kill) itself on caller death. candidate.target: Private replacement for telegram_http_ffi.erl implementing the SAME request/6 API (Method, Url, Headers, Body, TimeoutMs, MaxBytes). Not adopted.
candidate.architecture: Three processes, one owned connection. caller monitors guardian; guardian owns and kills the exact conn, monitors the actual caller, and performs NO blocking network call; a separate worker performs every blocking call. The guardian hands the exact conn pid to the caller BEFORE any I/O, so the caller can reap it if the guardian itself dies.

invariants.I1: Guardian takes ownership of the exact connection pid BEFORE any network I/O, via hackney_conn_sup:start_conn(ConnOpts#{owner => self()}), and hands that pid to the caller immediately.
invariants.I2: Guardian performs no blocking network call. It selects on messages plus a deadline only, so it stays responsive while the worker blocks.
invariants.I3: Cleanup is exit(Pid,kill) on the exact worker and the exact conn, with bounded DOWN confirmation. kill is untrappable, so cleanup never depends on a blocked connection processing a DOWN, an EXIT or any message. No hackney_conn:stop/1 and no hackney:close/1, so no proc_lib:stop and no gen:do_call at infinity.
invariants.I4: Guard-death race: the caller holds the conn pid from the handoff and reaps it when the guardian dies.
invariants.I5: Body bytes are capped INCREMENTALLY during {async, once} streaming using request_async/8 with StreamTo set to the worker, plus stream_next/1 per message. body/2 whole-body retrieval is deliberately NOT used.

preserved_policies: Host header: computed by compute_netloc inside hackney_conn:init/1, preserved by construction.
Content-Length: declared length checked against MaxBytes at the headers message, and the running accumulation checked per chunk.
No redirects: request_async is called with FollowRedirect = false explicitly.
TLS: scheme https maps to hackney_ssl and ssl_options are passed through in ConnOpts exactly as hackney.erl does. NOT VERIFIED - see G-1.
Bootstrap: ensure_started/1 is a separate bounded export. request/6 never starts hackney; it returns hackney_not_started if hackney_conn_sup is absent.

test_results.expected_noise: Each abort emits a SUPERVISOR REPORT from hackney_conn_sup with child_terminated and reason killed. hackney_conn children are restart_type temporary, so no restart occurs. The global logger was NOT changed to suppress these.

gaps.gap: TLS is NOT verified. No TLS server fixture was stood up, so certificate verification, SNI, and the ssl_options pass-through are unexercised. The one https case only proves the path fails closed against a closed port.
gaps.needed: A private TLS fixture with a known certificate, asserting that verification is actually enforced and that a bad certificate is refused.

gaps.gap: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 are untested. hackney 3.2.1 contains separate checkout_h2 and checkout_h3 paths and protocol negotiation; whether the guardian protocol composes with them is unknown.
Pooling is untested. The candidate passes no pool option and terminates the conn on every path, which is correct only while there is no reuse.

The guardian-death test locates the guardian by scanning erlang:processes/0 for current_function {_,guardian_loop,7}. That is adequate for a private test but is not how production would identify it; a registered or supervised guardian identity would be needed for a real cancellation API.
The 250 ms reap budget, the 1000 ms handoff budget and the 500 ms caller slack are chosen values with no measurement behind them.
No long-run soak, so file-descriptor and ETS behaviour under repeated kills is unmeasured.

A guardian that dies BEFORE the handoff leaves a conn that only its own owner monitor can reap, which is the very mechanism X2 shows is unreliable when the conn is blocked. The window is narrow because start_conn is the guardian's first act and the handoff is its third, but it is not closed. Recorded rather than papered over.
